thread:
maya: heads-up — we just got an SLO burn alert for hosted inference eu-west-1. Probe error rate spiked to ~12% starting ~02:28 UTC, customers reporting timeouts. Alert: https://console.redwood/alerts/INC-2141 :disappointed:

sre-bot: [auto] SLO_ALERT: /v1/generate p50 latency > 1s and 5xx rate > 5% over 5m in eu-west-1. Pager: oncall-maya.

kevin: putting my screen share on. initial look at edge-proxy shows a lot of `TLS handshake failed` / `connection reset by peer` from a cluster of client IPs but also a spike in 502/504 upstreams. Not pure auth issue.

aditya: can you paste the prom query you're eyeballing? I'll cross-check runtime node metrics.

kevin: here's the quick query I used in grafana:```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",job="edge-proxy",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
```
we see 5xx concentrated on 3 edge instances: edge-07/08/09.

maya: support-bot just forwarded an escalated customer case — they saw repeated 504s during a batch inference run and then billing showed a bunch of partial charges. Customer says retries didn't succeed.

support-bot: case #C-9921: customer used batching client with aggressive retry backoff=0.5s, concurrency 64. Logs show repeated 504s and then aborted requests. I attached their client logs.

zack: looking at ingress tcpstats on edge-07. There's a sudden jump in `half_open` and `syn_retries`. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion or kernel-level accept queue overflow. Also seeing `EMFILE` in the edge-proxy process logs.

aditya: interesting — on the runtime side (gpu-pool) most nodes are fine, CPU/queue looks stable. But I do see increased latency for model load on a subset of pods which coincides with a KV-cache miss storm. Could be thundering-herd when a small set of prefixes get cold.

maya: so multiple factors: client retries + batch cold cache + edge accept limits. We need a mitigation path ASAP.

kevin: temp mitigation ideas: 1) enable per-instance connection backpressure (limit new conn rate) 2) route traffic away from edge-07/08/09 via proxy ring routing 3) flip the model fallback to the smaller quantized variant for eu-west-1 to reduce load per request.

aditya: I can flip fallback to quantized-llama-lite now. That will reduce GPU memory churn. Give me 2m.

aditya: done. Routing rule updated:```
PATCH /routing/policies/evict-edge-07-09
{"preferred_instances": ["edge-*"], "exclude": ["edge-07","edge-08","edge-09"]}
```

kevin: I'm cordoning edge-07/08/09 from LB and draining. Doing `kubectl cordon/drain` now.

zack: also raising ephemeral port range on edge nodes and bumping `somaxconn` to 1024 to reduce accept queue drops. Pushing sysctl via orchestration:```
echo 1024 > /proc/sys/net/core/somaxconn
echo "1024 65000" > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
```

maya: after routing change + cordon we see 5xx rate drop from 12% -> 2.1% in the last 2m. Probe SLO trending down. Thanks.

kevin: one concern: traces are missing for many of the failed requests — there are gaps where trace IDs exist in edge but no downstream runtime spans. Looks like the request never reached runtime or failed during TLS. Need to instrument packet-level drops.

aditya: on runtime logs I see `error: tls handshake aborted` around the same timestamps — likely client side closing connections mid-handshake due to tight retry windows.

support-bot: customer updated: after we retried with exponential backoff they saw much better success. They also requested explanation for partial billing — can we route to billing/sales with a note?

maya: yes please attach timeline + mitigation. I'll draft a brief for CS. Action items: [1] postmortem draft, [2] dashboard panel for edge accept queue and EMFILE alerts, [3] recommend client-side retry budget with jitter, [4] investigate KV-cache pre-warming for high-traffic prefixes.

zack: filing infra task to increase node ephemeral ports and add sysctl guardrails (infra#987).

kevin: follow-up: add a lightweight synthetic that simulates bursty batch clients (concurrency=64, backoff=0.5s) to our chaos suite to catch this earlier. I'll add it to eng-sre/chaos.

maya: ok, last check: SLOs are recovering, but we'll keep monitoring for 30m. I'll claim the postmortem and coordinate with support for the billing note. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: [auto] Incident RESOLVED (eu-west-1): 5xx spike mitigated, routing/drain applied. Follow-up tasks assigned.
